subject: illustration
intro: Illustration leads into the image-making trades: the artists who draw for publication, the graphic designers who solve visual problems, the animators who move pictures, and the art directors who steer them all.

roles.title: Fine Artists, Including Painters, Sculptors, and Illustrators
roles.what: Create original artwork using a wide variety of media and techniques — on commission for clients and publications, for galleries, or built around a personal body of work sold directly.
roles.where: Units 1 and 2 are the toolkit: observational drawing, composition and visual storytelling, and fluency in traditional media such as ink, watercolour and gouache alongside digital workflows.

roles.title: Graphic Designers
roles.what: Design or create graphics to meet specific commercial or promotional needs — packaging, displays, logos and campaigns — using illustration and typography to solve a client's visual problem.
roles.where: Unit 5's advertising and packaging topics and unit 2's digital tools and colour theory for illustrators are the daily material of commercial design work.

roles.title: Special Effects Artists and Animators
roles.what: Create special effects or animations using film, video, computers and other electronic media for computer games, movies, music videos and commercials.
roles.where: Unit 5's motion and animation crossover unit is the direct bridge, built on unit 4's character design and sequential storytelling and unit 2's digital workflows.

roles.title: Art Directors
roles.what: Formulate design concepts and presentation approaches for visual productions and media such as print, broadcasting, video and film, and direct the artists and designers who produce the artwork.
roles.where: Unit 3's working with art directors becomes running the desk: judging concept generation, metaphor and visual argument against a brief, with unit 6's contracts, pricing and licensing as the business frame.
